topics: renewal term; EU private deployment; APAC burst; dedicated vs hosted; KMS/HSM; SOC2; pricing; next steps
transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-08-09 16:00 UTC; Duration: 46 mins; Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (Head of ML Ops - AstraNova), Priya Patel (CTO - AstraNova), Liam O'Neill (SRE - AstraNova)

Summary: quick check-in on renewal and expansion. Customer usage up ~2.6x y/y; wants region redundancy and EU on-prem-ish VPC for PII traffic. Agreed scope: 12 month term + EU private pilot + APAC burst arrangement.

00:00 - Jordan Park: Alright everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll do a quick... quick run through the renewal ask and the region expansion. Maya and I will talk through numbers and then we'll go to the tech asks.
00:14 - Tom Alvarez: Yeah thanks, Jordan. Quick context: we've been seeing, uh, peak inference at about 45 TPS on the payment fraud model, token average maybe 320 per call. We're seeing latency spikes at evenings for EU users at about 420 ms p95 which is not great for the checkout flow.
00:38 - Maya Singh: Got it. That's consistent with what we saw in the perf report. So, to clarify, you're currently on Hosted with dedicated burst? or is it Dedicated capacity? (laughs) sorry, I'm mixing up -
00:52 - Tom Alvarez: We're on the reserved dedicated pool, yes. It's a mix — reserved for baseline and then we hit hosted burst when we exceed the pool. The problem is cross-region egress and the EU residency — we need an EU Private node because of GDPR-probably-some... yeah.
01:20 - Priya Patel: And to add, legally we need KMS key control for some PII logs. So HSM or customer-managed KMS. It's a must-have for the renewal.
01:33 - Jordan Park: Yep totally. So options we laid out: 1) continue dedicated + hosted burst, 2) add EU Private (VPC) deployment with customer-managed KMS, 3) full on-prem pilot (longer lead time). Tradeoffs are lead time and cost. Maya, can you walk perf differences?
01:50 - Maya Singh: Sure. For the fraud model we saw on our test runs the EU private nodes reduce cross-region latency by ~80-90 ms p95; if we collocate the KV cache and enable prefix caching you'll get another ~30-40 ms. Cost-wise private adds a premium because of reserved capacity and ddos/hardening overheads but per-token cost often drops when we enable aggressive batching and quantization profiles.
02:25 - Liam O'Neill: Wait sorry, quantization — we're worried about quality drift. What's the QA on 4-bit or 8-bit for our model? We can't have false negatives on fraud detection.
02:36 - Maya Singh: Yep totally—good call. We'll run a side-by-side eval with your prompt set. For fraud models the recall drop was <0.6% in our last micro-bench on the 8-bit path, but we'll validate with your test set. Also there's a rollback path to switch to full FP16 in canary if we see regressions.
03:05 - Tom Alvarez: Okay. Timeline wise, we need the EU nodes live before Oct 1 ideally. Is that feasible?
03:15 - Jordan Park: It's tight but doable as a pilot - EU VPC pilot with a subset of capacity we can aim for late September. We should plan for a benchmark run next week. Maya?
03:25 - Maya Singh: Yeah I can start the benchmark week of Aug 16. I'll need the sample prompts and a traffic replay or TSV of request timing. Tom, Priya can you share that by Aug 13?
03:38 - Priya Patel: Yes, we'll put that together.
03:43 - Jordan Park: On pricing — we're proposing a 12-month renewal with a blended rate, plus a one-off onboarding fee for EU private. We'll run numbers and put a revised quote by Aug 12.
03:57 - Tom Alvarez: Are there comparable offers from competitors, like CloudModelCo doing something similar? They quoted lower per-token but no SOC2 pro? That was their pitch.
04:10 - Jordan Park: Right CloudModelCo tends to focus on list price, less on compliance ops. Also note our console gives token-level tracing, costs, and per-route throttles which customers lean on. We'll include an appendix showing e2e latency and cost tradeoffs.
04:35 - Maya Singh: Tech note — VPC onboarding requires IP allowlist, peering or private link. Liam, which topology do you prefer? NAT + firewall or a privatelink style?
04:47 - Liam O'Neill: Prefer privatelink equivalent but we may have to run it through our firewall team. We'll get specifics.
05:00 - Tom Alvarez: Also, do you support SAML SSO and SCIM for RBAC? We want role separation for dev vs infra.
05:09 - Jordan Park: Yes, SAML SSO, SCIM and fine-grained RBAC are supported. We'll share the SSO setup guide.
05:18 - Priya Patel: Also need the SOC 2 Type II attestations and pen test reports.
05:23 - Maya Singh: We'll send SOC2 Type II PDF and a redacted pentest summary; full pentest under NDA if needed.
05:35 - Tom Alvarez: On legal — our procurement wants a 12-month term but with a 60-day exit clause tied to SLA misses. Thoughts?
05:45 - Jordan Park: We can discuss contract language; typical is term with service credits. Jordan (AE) to loop legal to talk SLA thresholds. We'll flag this to Contract Ops.
06:02 - Maya Singh: For benchmarking, I'll run three profiles — low latency (small batch), balanced, and cost-optimized (larger batch). We'll measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
06:18 - Liam O'Neill: On monitoring — do you expose per-route traces and token-level cost in the console or via API? We need programmatic alerts.
06:27 - Maya Singh: Both. Console shows dashboards and you can pull via billing API. We'll add tracing hooks to your observability stack, e.g., DataDog or Prometheus.
06:42 - Tom Alvarez: Great. Can you include a sample of the logs we get and retention settings? We need 7 years for audit logs — that's in scope?
06:52 - Jordan Park: Seven years is long — standard retention on hosted is 90 days, extended retention is an add-on. For EU private or Dedicated you can export logs to your S3 and retain as long as your policy requires. We'll note that in the doc.
07:10 - Priya Patel: What's realistic on lead times for KMS integrations? We need customer-managed keys and rotation policies.
07:19 - Maya Singh: KMS/CD integration depends on provider. For AWS KMS with cross-account keys, typical is 2-3 weeks for validation; for HSM it's longer. We'll provide a runbook.
07:32 - Jordan Park: Ok, let's recap - agreed next actions: Redwood to run benchmarks (Aug 16 week), customer to share prompt set by Aug 13, Redwood to send revised quote by Aug 12, Legal touchpoint to draft amendment by Aug 23, and pilot target late Sept. Anything else?
07:55 - Tom Alvarez: One more: can you show us a pricing sensitivity for 6 vs 12 month term? We may prefer a 6-month to hedge.
08:05 - Jordan Park: Yep will include 6 vs 12 month scenarios in the quote.
08:12 - Priya Patel: Also, we want an escalation contact for ops during onboarding.
08:16 - Jordan Park: We'll assign a CSM and provide contact. I'll include CSM name in the document.
08:24 - Liam O'Neill: Ok thanks. That's all from infra side.
08:28 - Jordan Park: Great thank you all. We'll follow up with the doc and benchmark schedule. Thanks.
08:35 - (Call ends)

Notes: Transcript has some ASR artifacts: 'V-B-C' = VPC, 'KV cash' = KV cache, 'HSM' misread sometimes. Action items summarized above.
